why: B has three parts: (R) the restriction to an open V ∋ x₀ with x₀ arbitrary, (L) Lemma 9.1.7, (C) the J = I × G_x construction for any natural-representation datum (IsNatRepData) on an open U ⊆ U'. A has Lemma 9.1.7 with U(x) inside any given V (lemma_9_1_7, lemma_9_1_7') and general facts (isClosed_M, isProperMap_inclusion_iff, apply_Φ). A_to_B gets (L) from lemma_9_1_7': the NaturalRep becomes IsNatRepData and the MulAction becomes IsActionB. (R) and (C) are not in A's theorems: A's restrict (V ∋ x only) and symmetrize (it takes a NaturalRep, whose U is connected) are only vocabulary, so both are re-proved here. They are about 60 lines of glue following the project's symmetrize, with no new mathematics. B_to_A gets lemma_9_1_7 from B (C): take a structure at x and a NaturalRep R ⊆ U(x) ∩ V (theorem_7_1, Chapter 7), then repackage the result as a SymmetricBranchingStructure, with the MulAction on I × G_x built from B's IsActionB. lemma_9_1_7' follows from it, and the general facts are re-proved outright. Neither side is stronger in content: B's (R) for arbitrary x₀ and (C) for non-connected U are true and provable from the project's lemmas. Universes: 0.
